microtheory.name: political_science
microtheory.definition: Political science — power, governance, institutions, political behavior. Aristotle, Hobbes, Locke, Rousseau, Marx, Weber, Schmitt, Arendt, Rawls. Comparative politics, IR, political theory, public policy, political economy. Substrate analogue: the discipline of collective decision-making + power-distribution.

concepts.name: power_political
concepts.definition: Capacity to influence others' behavior despite resistance (Weber). Three faces: decision (Dahl), agenda (Bachrach+Baratz), thought (Lukes).

concepts.name: authority
concepts.definition: Legitimate power. Weber's typology: traditional, charismatic, rational-legal. Substrate analogue: substrate's accepted-rule basis.

concepts.name: legitimacy
concepts.definition: Acceptance by ruled. Belief that authority is rightful. Distinct from legality. Substrate analogue: substrate's accepted-validity.

concepts.name: sovereignty
concepts.definition: Ultimate authority within territory. Westphalian state system 1648. Increasingly contested by transnational forces.

concepts.name: state
concepts.definition: Weber: human community claiming monopoly of legitimate violence over territory. Modern, bureaucratic, territorial.

concepts.name: hobbes_leviathan
concepts.definition: Thomas Hobbes 1651. State of nature = war of all against all. Social contract surrenders right of self-defense to sovereign for protection.

concepts.name: locke_natural_rights
concepts.definition: John Locke. Life, liberty, property as pre-political rights. Government legitimate only when protects them. Right of revolution.

concepts.name: rousseau_general_will
concepts.definition: Jean-Jacques Rousseau. Volonté générale — what people would will if seeking common good. Republican tradition.

concepts.name: montesquieu_separation_powers
concepts.definition: Spirit of the Laws 1748. Executive, legislative, judicial separated → liberty preserved. US Constitution.

concepts.name: arendt_human_condition
concepts.definition: Hannah Arendt. Political action distinct from labor + work. Public space + plurality required for freedom.

concepts.name: rawls_justice_as_fairness
concepts.definition: John Rawls 1971. Original position behind veil of ignorance. Two principles: equal basic liberties + difference principle (inequalities benefit worst-off).

concepts.name: schmitt_political_theology
concepts.definition: Carl Schmitt. The political = friend/enemy distinction. Sovereign decides on exception.

concepts.name: democracy
concepts.definition: Rule by the people. Direct (Athens) or representative (modern). Procedural (elections) + substantive (rights, deliberation). Schumpeter vs Dahl definitions.

concepts.name: republic
concepts.definition: Res publica. Non-monarchical government, often with rights-based constitution. Mixed: democracy + aristocracy + monarchy elements.

concepts.name: authoritarianism
concepts.definition: Concentrated power, limited political pluralism, no genuine accountability. Linz typology.

concepts.name: totalitarianism
concepts.definition: Arendt + Friedrich. Total ideological mobilisation, mass party, terror, state economy. Nazi + Stalinist extremes.

concepts.name: monarchy
concepts.definition: Rule by single hereditary ruler. Absolute (Louis XIV) vs constitutional (UK).

concepts.name: ideology
concepts.definition: System of ideas justifying + critiquing political order. Liberalism, conservatism, socialism, fascism, nationalism, environmentalism.

concepts.name: liberalism_political
concepts.definition: Individual rights + limited government + market economy + rule of law. Classical (Locke) → modern (Rawls) variants.

concepts.name: conservatism
concepts.definition: Burke + others. Skepticism of rapid change. Tradition + organic society + prudence. Right-Hegelian + Anglo-American variants.

concepts.name: socialism
concepts.definition: Collective ownership of means of production. Democratic socialism + Marxism + market socialism variants.

concepts.name: election
concepts.definition: Procedure for selecting officeholders. Plurality vs majority vs proportional vs ranked-choice systems.

concepts.name: representation_political
concepts.definition: Pitkin's typology: formal, descriptive, substantive, symbolic. Edmund Burke vs delegate views.

concepts.name: parliament
concepts.definition: Legislative body. Parliamentary vs presidential systems. Cabinet drawn from parliament (Westminster) vs separation of powers.

concepts.name: constitution
concepts.definition: Fundamental law constituting + limiting government. Written (US) vs unwritten (UK). Judicial review.

concepts.name: rule_of_law
concepts.definition: Government bound by law, equally applied. Predictability + non-arbitrariness.

concepts.name: civil_society
concepts.definition: Non-state non-market voluntary associations. Tocqueville. Counterweight to state + market.

concepts.name: public_sphere_habermas
concepts.definition: Jürgen Habermas. Space of rational-critical discussion grounding legitimate authority. Eroded by mass media commercialisation.

concepts.name: collective_action_problem
concepts.definition: Olson 1965. Free-rider problem. Why don't groups with common interest organise? Selective incentives, small numbers, coercion.

concepts.name: international_relations
concepts.definition: States as actors in anarchical system. Realism, liberalism, constructivism schools.

concepts.name: realism_ir
concepts.definition: Morgenthau, Waltz. States seek power + security under anarchy. Balance of power.

concepts.name: liberal_institutionalism
concepts.definition: Keohane + Nye. Institutions + interdependence + trade mitigate anarchy. Substrate analogue: substrate's institution-stabilised interaction.

concepts.name: constructivism_ir
concepts.definition: Wendt. Anarchy is what states make of it. Identities + norms constitute interests.

rules.name: power_legitimacy_distinction
rules.head: Jabberwock evaluates a political authority
rules.body: power (ability to coerce) and legitimacy (acceptance) are distinct. Stable authority requires legitimacy in addition to power. Weber. Substrate's accepted-rule distinction.

rules.name: separation_of_powers_protects_liberty
rules.head: Jabberwock designs a government structure
rules.body: executive + legislative + judicial separated → mutual check prevents tyranny. Montesquieu. Substrate's institutional-balance pattern.

rules.name: collective_action_requires_solving_free_rider
rules.head: Jabberwock observes large group with common interest
rules.body: rational individuals free-ride; group fails to organise unless selective incentives, small numbers, or coercion. Olson 1965.

rules.name: rule_of_law_constrains_arbitrary_power
rules.head: Jabberwock distinguishes lawful from arbitrary rule
rules.body: rule of law requires general + prospective + clear rules equally applied. Without it, no rights guarantee.

rules.name: anarchy_is_constructed_not_given
rules.head: Jabberwock analyses international system
rules.body: anarchy is constructed through identities + norms + interactions (Wendt). Not a fixed structure. Substrate's constructed-not-given international space.
